papers.title: Somnus, a tunable, open-source platform for automated EEG sleep scoring in physiological and disease mouse models.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Introduces Somnus, an open-source Python package for automated rodent sleep staging from EEG, EMG, and optional video, built on a base model trained across recordings from six laboratories. Its key contribution is a graphical interface that targets low-certainty epochs for rapid manual correction and fine-tuning, enabling accurate custom scorers for disease models with atypical sleep architecture using only minutes of manual annotation.

papers.title: BioLT: Streaming Biosignal Modeling
papers.summary: Introduces BioLT, a streaming decoder-only framework that converts window-level biosignal feature extractors or foundation models into long-context streaming models via discontinuity-aware encoding of inter-window elapsed time and a compressed memory bank. Across 21 dataset-feature settings on four datasets, BioLT achieved the highest detection AUROC in 15 and highest 20-minute forecasting AUROC in 13 settings.

papers.title: Advanced Two-Stage Authentication with EEG: Inter-Subject P300 ERP Classification Using EEGNet for User Recognition.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.summary: Proposes a two-stage EEG authentication framework combining multi-class user identification and binary authentication using P300 ERP features and EEGNet, with a preprocessing pipeline of filtering, epoch rejection, cropping, and downsampling. Across 16 participants and three sessions, the system reached up to 95% precision and a mean accuracy of 96.10% for identification and authentication.

papers.title: Enhancing the Suppression of Unwanted Memories During NREM Sleep.
papers.summary: Combined the Think/No-Think paradigm with targeted memory reactivation during NREM sleep to test whether reactivating suppression instructions modulates later forgetting. Sleep-cued suppression enhanced suppression-induced forgetting, and EEG showed increased theta power and reduced slow-oscillation up-state-spindle coupling, with reduced coupling predicting poorer later retrieval.

papers.title: Discrete cortico-hippocampal circuit states underlie mood state transitions in depression.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: Using precision functional mapping, large cross-sectional cohorts, and intracranial EEG, shows hippocampal connectivity alternates between discrete DMN-dominant and sensorimotor-dominant network states on the order of minutes. In major depressive disorder the DMN-dominant state is overrepresented, hippocampus-DMN coupling tracks symptom fluctuations, and electroconvulsive therapy shifts connectivity toward the SM-dominant state in association with positive treatment response.

papers.title: Feasibility of Vibrotactile P50 Sensory-Gating Assessment Using Portable EEG
papers.summary: Evaluated feasibility of a portable vibrotactile P50 sensory-gating paradigm against auditory gating in 15 healthy adults using 32-channel portable EEG. Vibrotactile stimulation elicited time-locked P50 responses with S2 attenuation, and mean S2/S1 ratios did not differ significantly between auditory (0.521) and vibrotactile (0.524) conditions.

papers.title: Coupled neuro-fluid dynamics in human bioelectromagnetism.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Using conductive-fluid phantom experiments, structural MRI, and in vivo EEG/MEG recordings, this study challenges the assumption that tissue and CSF are passive volume conductors. Mechanically driven fluid produced structured, source-localizable oscillatory electromagnetic signals resembling M/EEG, and interindividual CSF volume moderated M/EEG amplitude, suggesting coupled neuro-fluid dynamics.

papers.title: BiXCA-DualFormer: A time-frequency fusion model for epileptic seizure prediction.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers. Part H, Journal of engineering in medicine
papers.summary: Proposes BiXCA-DualFormer, a dual-branch time-frequency fusion model that processes raw EEG and short-time Fourier representations through separate temporal and spectral branches with bidirectional cross-attention, a Transformer encoder, and learnable query pooling for seizure prediction. On CHB-MIT it achieved 95.29% accuracy, 96.40% sensitivity, 95.05% specificity, and a 0.0495 false positive rate.

papers.title: Altered EEG-derived co-fluctuation structure in disorders of consciousness.
papers.summary: This study adapted an EEG-derived co-fluctuation framework to resting-state data, decomposing connectivity time series into high- and low-amplitude frames to characterize dynamic functional connectivity across consciousness levels. Loss of consciousness was associated with reduced co-fluctuation stability, a shift toward random system dynamics, and reduced spatial and temporal heterogeneity, with combined HAF/LAF parameters showing diagnostic potential for distinguishing DOC states.

papers.title: Distinguishing evidence accumulation from choice confidence in neural signatures of perceptual decision making
papers.summary: Using EEG with 80%-valid predictive cues in a contrast discrimination task, this study dissociated the centro-parietal positivity (CPP) from subjective confidence. Valid cues reduced pre-response CPP amplitude even when confidence was matched, supporting the CPP as an evidence accumulation signal contributing to both decision formation and confidence estimation rather than a direct read-out of confidence.

papers.title: Understanding Performance Plateaus and Representation Collapse in 3D MRI Transformers Trained to Classify Brain Disease.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Spectral analysis of supervised 3D vision transformers classifying Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative brain MRI showed that discriminative signal is compressed into a single dominant principal component (EVR@1 = 0.90–0.96), producing representation collapse and performance plateaus as training data increase. This spike was 11–26 times larger than predicted for supervised encoders but absent for the frozen self-supervised DINO encoder (0.66), and plateauing tracked the learned encoder rather than task difficulty.

papers.title: Probing the neural geometry of conscious object perception in time.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: High-density EEG during a threshold-level object recognition task revealed early (~100 ms) emergence of both basic- and superordinate-level category information, with basic-level category positively and superordinate-level negatively correlated with perceptual awareness. An abstract superordinate representation emerged later (~300 ms) and positively correlated with awareness, supporting a basic-to-superordinate sequence in conscious object perception.

papers.title: A Common Recognition Architecture Across Memory Scales
papers.summary: EEG during recognition memory tasks across set sizes of 1 to 128 items showed that frontal and parietal old/new effects persisted continuously across memory scales. Multivariate classifiers generalized across set sizes, and recognition signals followed a common waveform trajectory that emerged later and weaker at larger scales, with behavioral relevance shifting from working memory to long-term memory.

papers.title: Depressive status modulates hippocampal-cortical dynamics during acute nicotine use.
papers.summary: Using simultaneous hippocampal responsive neurostimulation electrodes and scalp EEG in two chronic nicotine users, one with and one without depression, this study found that oscillatory activity tracked mood only in the non-depressed individual, whereas both showed reduced alpha hippocampal-cortical connectivity after nicotine inhalation. The authors interpret this as preliminary evidence that depressive status may modulate nicotine-driven network dynamics.

papers.title: Aging Is Associated with Reduced Topographic Differentiation Between Speaking and Silent Reading.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: EEG comparison of 15 young and 15 older adults during speaking versus silent reading found similar global field power across groups but greater global dissimilarity index in young adults during later intervals (508–629 and 660–800 ms), indicating reduced neural differentiation between tasks with aging. Behavioral performance and correlations with digit span or speech onset time were not significant.

papers.title: Ion Channels and Morphology Drive Widespread Resonance in Human Cortical Interneurons.
papers.summary: Combining Patch-seq, acute electrophysiology, organotypic cultures, and computational modeling, this study found that membrane potential resonance is more prevalent in adult human cortical interneurons than in mouse interneurons, peaking in parvalbumin cells and correlating with low input resistance, voltage sag, and HCN1, KCNJ16, and CACNA1A expression. HCN blockade abolished resonance, and models showed human morphology and ion channels sharpen frequency tuning under in vivo-like noisy conditions.

papers.title: I err, therefore I am: Neural signature of error-monitoring predicts self-awareness in infants
papers.summary: In a longitudinal gaze-contingent match-to-sample paradigm with eye-tracking and EEG, 12-month-old infants showed an error-related negativity (ERN) after incorrect saccades and before feedback. ERN at 12 months predicted mirror self-recognition at 18 months, and only later self-recognizing infants adjusted behavior post-error, suggesting internal error-monitoring contributes to building conceptual self-awareness.

papers.title: Adaptive Spectral Analysis of Umbilical Venous Doppler Maternal-Fetal Power Ratio for Preeclampsia Risk Assessment.
papers.journal: Journal of ultrasound in medicine : official journal of the American Institute of Ultrasound in Medicine
papers.summary: This retrospective study developed adaptive spectral analysis of umbilical venous Doppler to derive the maternal-fetal power ratio (MFPR) and tested its association with subsequent preeclampsia in second-trimester recordings. Higher MFPR was associated with later preeclampsia, with best AUCs of 0.84 (heart-rate-guided adaptive Capon, short recordings) and 0.75 (heart-rate-guided Welch, long recordings).

papers.title: Optimisation of and mechanisms behind neural distortion responses obtained with cochlear-implant stimulation by interleaved pulse trains
papers.summary: Four EEG experiments in cochlear-implant users manipulated interleaved amplitude-modulated pulse trains to characterize neural distortion responses (NDRs), separating quadratic and cubic distortion products and varying phase and pulse polarity. NDRs contained both quadratic and cubic components and were largest when AM maxima aligned; computational modeling suggested refractoriness plays a stronger role than facilitation, though it did not fully explain polarity effects.

papers.title: Pre-synaptic facilitation of corticospinal output improves dexterity and finemotor control after stroke
papers.summary: In three monkeys with corticospinal tract lesions, deep brain stimulation of motor thalamus-to-primary motor cortex projections improved upper-limb strength and dexterous hand/digit control, enabling unconstrained 3D reach and fine motor tasks; electrophysiology suggested effects were mediated by fibers with monosynaptic connections to corticospinal motoneurons.

papers.title: A Human iPSC-Derived Neuron and Glioma Culture Model Reveals Increased Neuronal Excitability and Loss of GABAergic Inhibition.
papers.summary: Established a human iPSC-derived culture of glutamatergic neurons, GABAergic neurons, and astrocytes with and without glioma cells, characterized by immunocytochemistry, multi-electrode arrays, and patch-clamp. Glioma co-culture increased spike rate and network activity and reversed muscimol suppression into elevation of firing, indicating disrupted GABAergic inhibition and increased glutamatergic neuron excitability.

papers.title: Cellularized, needle-deployed intracortical arrays for brain electrophysiology.
papers.summary: Presents a hybrid implantation method combining a cellularized hydrogel with a neural recording array for simultaneous needle delivery into the brain. Post-implantation electrophysiological recordings demonstrated functional integration with surrounding neural tissue, supporting feasibility for coupled bioelectronic sensing and regenerative capability.

papers.title: Large-scale all-optical electrophysiology links excitability and connectivity to circuit dynamics in vivo.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Developed large-scale all-optical electrophysiology and applied it to about 300 layer 1 interneurons per mouse in vivo, identifying 1,469 inhibitory and 5,752 directed electrical connections across 14,312 tested pairs. Presynaptic identity related more to IPSP amplitude and postsynaptic identity more to IPSP decay, and measured intrinsic excitability predicted spontaneous spiking features.

papers.title: Technology and Intelligence: Staying on Target for the Next Decade of Electrophysiology.
papers.summary: This perspective discusses technological and intelligence-related developments anticipated in cardiac electrophysiology over the next decade, with emphasis on arrhythmia mechanisms, mapping, ablation, and cardiac pacing.

papers.title: The Clinical Profile and Bedside Clues of Anti-LGI1 Encephalitis Presenting With Isolated Cognitive Impairment: A Multicenter Retrospective Cohort Study.
papers.summary: In a multicenter retrospective cohort of 43 anti-LGI1 encephalitis patients presenting with isolated cognitive impairment, 69.8% evolved to broader neuropsychiatric syndromes (median latencies: psychiatric symptoms 21 days, FBDS 30 days, focal seizures 47.5 days), while 30.2% remained isolated; delayed recall impairment with preserved naming plus EEG/MRI abnormalities formed a practical bedside triad for early antibody screening.

papers.title: Deep Sedation in Single-Shot Pulmonary Vein Isolation: A Head-to-Head Look at Two Pulsed Field Versus Cryoballoon Ablation Approaches.
papers.summary: In a propensity-matched single-center study of 156 patients undergoing single-shot pulmonary vein isolation under deep sedation, pentaspline pulsed field ablation required higher weight- and time-adjusted propofol (0.15 vs 0.10-0.11 mg/kg/min) but had the shortest procedural and fluoroscopy times, while balloon-in-basket PFA showed reduced normalized sedative requirements and safety comparable to cryoballoon.

papers.title: Avermectin poisoning with panic-like symptoms: a case series.
papers.summary: Two case reports describe avermectin poisoning after oral ingestion and intramuscular injection, with toxic effects including respiratory failure, hypotension, acidosis, coma, delirium, and subsequent panic-like symptoms that improved with psychiatric care and supportive treatment.

papers.title: Transient HBV entry into cerebrospinal fluid following blood-brain barrier disruption: a case of HSV-2 encephalitis with polymicrobial detection elucidated by serial targeted next-generation sequencing.
papers.summary: In a case report of HSV-2 encephalitis with acute blood-brain barrier disruption, serial CSF targeted next-generation sequencing detected HSV-2, HHV-4, and HBV, and repeat sequencing after acyclovir and tenofovir alafenamide showed synchronous clearance of all three viruses alongside normalized CSF parameters and restored BBB integrity, supporting transient passive HBV entry into CSF rather than true CNS coinfection.

papers.title: Excitation-contraction coupling plasticity is revealed upon RyR2 depletion in adult mouse ventricular myocytes.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Used an adult tamoxifen-inducible RyR2 conditional knockout mouse to test whether excitation-contraction coupling adapts to acute RyR2 loss. Hearts with <10% residual RyR2 maintained normal structure, function, Ca2+ transient amplitude, and ECC gain via elevated SR Ca2+ load, high channel reserve, and CaT autoregulation, revealing intrinsic ECC plasticity.

papers.title: 5-HT1A Antagonist WAY-100635 Prevents Chronic Neurodegeneration and Immune Activation After TBI.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Tested post-injury WAY-100635, a 5-HT1A antagonist, in mice after controlled cortical impact and found it preserved retinal ganglion cell survival and visual function, maintained visually evoked cortical responses, and reduced microglial activation and reactive astrogliosis. Treatment also improved early motor performance and reduced injury-associated behavioral disinhibition without significantly reducing cortical cavity volume.

papers.title: Heteroatom effects on tricyclic fused aromatic molecules revealed by rotational spectroscopy.
papers.summary: Using chirped-pulse Fourier transform microwave spectroscopy (2-18 GHz) assisted by MP2 and B3LYP-D3(BJ) calculations, the authors assigned rotational spectra and heavy-atom isotopologues of dibenzothiophene, dibenzofuran, and carbazole and determined their experimental structures via rs, r0, rSEe, and r(1)m methods, revealing heteroatom-driven structural and electronic changes within the fluorene scaffold.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
